title: Irreducible components of a smooth variety do not meet
statement:
Let $X$ be an affine scheme of finite type over a field $k$ whose local
ring at every closed point is regular (for instance a smooth affine
variety). Then any two distinct irreducible components of $X$ are
disjoint. Consequently the (finitely many) irreducible components of $X$
are open and closed, and are its connected components.

proof.text: Put $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and identify the affine scheme $X$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A$. The finite-type structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ makes $A$ a finitely generated $k$-algebra by [lem-pc-affine-finite-type-algebra]. If $X$ is empty, it has no nonempty irreducible or connected components and all conclusions are vacuous; hence assume it is nonempty.

source.place: Tag 01T2, lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize, (1) implies (2), applied to the affine pair X and Spec k; blueprint proof, opening sentence

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes], write any two components as $C_i=V(\mathfrak p_i)$ with $\mathfrak p_i$ minimal prime ideals. If they meet, a prime $\mathfrak q$ in their intersection contains both $\mathfrak p_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal], choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\supseteq\mathfrak q$. Thus $\mathfrak p_1,\mathfrak p_2\subseteq\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tag 00ES, lemma-irreducible, (3); Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology, (2) and proof of (8); blueprint proof, first paragraph

proof.text: The point $x=\mathfrak m$ is closed: the closed set $V(\mathfrak m)$ equals $\{\mathfrak m\}$, since no proper prime strictly contains a maximal ideal. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] to the affine open $U=X$ identifies $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with $A_{\mathfrak m}$. The former is regular by the stated hypothesis, so [lem-sc-regular-local-domain] makes it, and hence $A_{\mathfrak m}$, a nonzero integral domain.

source.place: Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves, (6), and Algebra Tag 00NP, lemma-regular-domain; blueprint proof, first paragraph

proof.text: Let $\lambda:A\to A_{\mathfrak m}$ and $K=\ker\lambda$. Since $A_{\mathfrak m}$ is a nonzero domain, $K$ is proper and prime: $\lambda(ab)=0$ implies $\lambda(a)=0$ or $\lambda(b)=0$. For either $\mathfrak p_i$, if $a\in K$, the fraction equality criterion of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] gives $sa=0$ for some $s\notin\mathfrak m$. Then $sa\in\mathfrak p_i$ and $s\notin\mathfrak p_i$, so primality gives $a\in\mathfrak p_i$. Thus $K\subseteq\mathfrak p_i$; minimality of $\mathfrak p_i$ among prime ideals implies $K=\mathfrak p_i$. Consequently $\mathfrak p_1=\mathfrak p_2$ and $C_1=C_2$. This proves distinct components are disjoint.

source.place: First paragraph: the localization contradiction; expanded using the fraction equality criterion instead of invoking preservation of minimal primes without a citation

proof.text: By [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components] there are finitely many irreducible components $C_1,\ldots,C_r$. They are closed by [def-weil-irreducible-components], and they cover $X$ by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover]. The disjointness just proved gives $X\setminus C_j=\bigcup_{i\ne j}C_i$. This finite union of closed sets is closed; hence every $C_j$ is both open and closed.

source.place: Second paragraph, first two sentences: finiteness, covering, and the complement of a component

proof.text: Each $C_j$ is nonempty and irreducible, so [lem-pc-irreducible-space-connected] makes it connected. For $x\in C_j$, let $D_x$ be the connected component supplied by [lem-sfb-connected-component-maximality]. Its maximality gives $C_j\subseteq D_x$. If $D_x$ met $X\setminus C_j$, the two relatively clopen sets $D_x\cap C_j$ and $D_x\setminus C_j$ would be nonempty and partition $D_x$, contradicting connectedness. Thus $D_x=C_j$. Finally every point lies in a $C_j$ by step 5, so these are exactly all connected components.

lean.statement: theorem components_of_regular_closed_points {k : Type u} [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] (hreg : ∀ x : X, x ∈ closedPoints X → IsRegularLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x)) : (irreducibleComponents X).Finite ∧ (irreducibleComponents X).Pairwise Disjoint ∧ (∀ C ∈ irreducibleComponents X, IsClopen C) ∧ irreducibleComponents X = Set.range (fun x : X => connectedComponent x)
